libraries.title: bit
libraries.doc: Bitwise operations on 32-bit words, compatible with Lua's `bit32`. Arguments are reduced to their low 32 bits, so negative numbers act as their two's-complement words, and results are unsigned unless noted. For 64-bit and arbitrary-precision integers use the operators `&`, `|`, `~`, `<<`, `>>`, `<<<` and `>>>` instead.

libraries.title: buffer
libraries.doc:
Fixed-size blocks of mutable bytes for binary data: file formats, network protocols, hashing input. Offsets are 0-based byte positions and every access is bounds-checked. Numbers are little-endian unless the optional last argument `bigEndian` is `true`. Writing an integer that does not fit keeps its low bits.

```lua
local b = buffer.create(8)
buffer.writeu16(b, 0, 0xCAFE, true) -- big-endian
buffer.writef32(b, 2, 1.5)
print(buffer.tohex(b)) --> cafe0000c03f0000
```

libraries.title: coroutine
libraries.doc:
Functions that can pause in the middle and continue later. A coroutine runs until it calls `coroutine.yield`, which hands values back to whoever resumed it; the next `resume` continues right after the `yield`. They are handy for generators, state machines and cooperative tasks.

```lua
local counter = coroutine.wrap(function()
    for i = 1, 3 do coroutine.yield(i) end
end)
print(counter(), counter(), counter()) --> 1	2	3
```

A coroutine can only yield from its own Neyuki frames: yielding from inside a function that a native called back (a `try` body, a `table.sort` comparator, a metamethod) raises an error.

libraries.title: @neyuki/crypto
libraries.doc:
Hashing, password storage, encryption, signatures and secure random values, built on the RustCrypto and dalek crates so keys do not leak through timing and bulk work runs at native speed.

Binary values are strings in an *encoding*: `"hex"`, `"base64"` or `"base64url"`. Digests default to hex and everything else (keys, ciphertexts, signatures, random bytes) to base64. Asymmetric keys are PEM strings (PKCS#8 private, SPKI public) that OpenSSL and other languages read; PKCS#1 `RSA PRIVATE KEY` files are accepted too.

```lua
local crypto = require("@neyuki/crypto")

-- storing and checking a password
local stored = crypto.hashPassword("correct horse battery staple")
assert(crypto.verifyPassword("correct horse battery staple", stored))

-- encrypting a record, bound to its id
local key = crypto.generateKey()
local sealed = crypto.encrypt("card ending 4242", key, { aad = "user:42" })
print(crypto.decrypt(sealed, key, { aad = "user:42" }))
```

libraries.title: debug
libraries.doc: Introspection of the running program: stack traces, frame and function information, locals, upvalues and hooks. Levels count outward from the function calling the debug function: level 1 is that function, level 2 its caller, and so on.

libraries.title: @neyuki/fs
libraries.doc:
Files, directories and paths. Text files are read and written as UTF-8 strings.

```lua
local fs = require("@neyuki/fs")

fs.write("notes.txt", "first line\n")
fs.append("notes.txt", "second line\n")
for line in fs.lines("notes.txt") do print(line) end

for _, path in fs.walk("src") do
    if fs.extension(path) == ".nyk" then print(path, fs.info(fs.join("src", path)).size) end
end
```

libraries.title: Globals
libraries.doc: Functions available everywhere without `require`. The standard libraries (`math`, `string`, `table`, `bit`, `buffer`, `coroutine`, `utf8`, `debug`, `json`, `os`) are globals too; the `@neyuki/...` modules are loaded with `require`.

libraries.title: @neyuki/hid
libraries.doc:
Keyboard and mouse automation, screen size and the clipboard. Input goes to whichever window has focus, exactly as if a person typed or clicked. It works on Windows, macOS and X11 (Wayland sessions need XWayland); macOS asks for accessibility permission the first time.

Keys are single characters (`"a"`, `"7"`, `"/"`) or case-insensitive names: `enter`, `tab`, `space`, `backspace`, `delete`, `escape`, `up`, `down`, `left`, `right`, `home`, `end`, `pageup`, `pagedown`, `shift`, `ctrl`, `alt`, `meta` (also `win`, `cmd`, `super`), `capslock`, `f1` to `f20`, `numpad0` to `numpad9`, `volumeup`, `volumedown`, `mute`, `playpause`, `nexttrack` and `prevtrack`. Mouse buttons are `"left"` (the default), `"right"`, `"middle"`, `"back"` and `"forward"`. Coordinates are pixels from the top-left corner of the main display.

```lua
local hid = require("@neyuki/hid")

local w, h = hid.screen.size()
hid.mouse.glide(w / 2, h / 2)
hid.mouse.click()
hid.keyboard.write("Hello from Neyuki")
hid.keyboard.combo("ctrl+a")
hid.keyboard.combo("ctrl+c")
os.sleep(0.1)
print(hid.clipboard.get())
```

libraries.title: @neyuki/http
libraries.doc:
An HTTP/1.1 client and server, with TLS through the operating system's own library. Bodies are strings; response bytes that are not valid UTF-8 are replaced with U+FFFD. The runtime is single-threaded, so one script cannot serve and request itself at the same time.

```lua
local http = require("@neyuki/http")

local response = http.get("https://api.github.com/repos/neyuki-lang/neyuki", {
    headers = { ["user-agent"] = "neyuki" },
    timeout = 10,
})
if response.ok then
    print(json.decode(response.body).stargazers_count)
end
```

libraries.title: @neyuki/io
libraries.doc:
Reading from and writing to the terminal (standard input, output and error) for interactive scripts and command-line filters.

```lua
local io = require("@neyuki/io")

local name = io.prompt("What is your name? ")
io.write("Hello, ", name, "!\n")

-- a filter: number every line piped in
local n = 0
for line in io.lines() do
    n += 1
    io.write(n, ": ", line, "\n")
end
```

libraries.title: json
libraries.doc:
Reading and writing JSON. Tables with only an array part become JSON arrays and every other table an object; integers stay exact and other numbers become floats.

```lua
local text = json.encode({ name = "neyuki", tags = { "small", "fast" } })
print(text) --> {"name":"neyuki","tags":["small","fast"]}
local data = json.decode(text)
print(data.tags[2]) --> fast
```

libraries.title: math
libraries.doc: Numbers, rounding, trigonometry and random values. Integers are exact and unbounded; functions that round (`floor`, `ceil`, `round`, `trunc`) return integers, and functions that compute (`sqrt`, `sin`, `log`, ...) return floats.

libraries.title: os
libraries.doc: Time, the environment, command-line arguments and the process.

libraries.title: @neyuki/profile
libraries.doc:
A simple profiler that counts calls and measures the time spent in each function, to find what makes a script slow.

```lua
local profile = require("@neyuki/profile")

profile.start()
runSimulation()
print(profile.stop())
-- runSimulation: calls=1, time=0.84s
-- step: calls=1000, time=0.81s
-- ...
```

libraries.title: @neyuki/sql
libraries.doc:
PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB through pure-Rust drivers, with TLS through the operating system's own library.

```lua
local sql = require("@neyuki/sql")
local db = sql.connect(os.getenv("DATABASE_URL"))

db:execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL)")
local user = db:queryOne("INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES ($1) RETURNING id", { "Ada" })

for _, row in db:query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY id") do
    print(row.id, row.name)
end
db:close()
```

Parameters are positional in the server's own syntax (`$1, $2` on PostgreSQL, `?` on MySQL) and are sent separately from the SQL text, so values are never spliced into it. A parameter may be `nil` (NULL), a boolean, a number or a string.

Results keep their types: integers stay integers, floats stay floats, PostgreSQL booleans are booleans (MySQL's are `0` and `1`), text is a string and a PostgreSQL array is an array. `numeric`/`decimal` come back as strings so no digit is rounded; dates, times, timestamps, `uuid` and `json` come back in their text form (`timestamptz` in UTC). A NULL column is absent from its row. Types the module does not know (`interval`, `inet`, ranges, composites) raise an error naming them; cast them to `text` in the query.

libraries.title: string
libraries.doc:
Text functions. Every string also has these as methods, so `s:upper()` is `string.upper(s)`. Strings are UTF-8 and indices are byte positions starting at 1; negative indices count from the end (`-1` is the last byte). `#s` and `string.len` count bytes, `string.count` counts characters.

Patterns follow Lua: `.` any character, `%a` letters, `%d` digits, `%s` whitespace, `%w` letters and digits, `%p` punctuation, `%l`/`%u` lower and upper case (capitalized classes such as `%S` negate), `[set]` and `[^set]`, the quantifiers `*`, `+`, `-` (lazy) and `?`, the anchors `^` and `$`, captures `( )`, `%b()` for balanced pairs and `%f[set]` for frontiers. `%` escapes a special character.

libraries.title: table
libraries.doc: Functions for arrays (tables with keys 1, 2, 3, ...) and other tables. `#t` is the length of the array part; `table.length` counts every entry.

libraries.title: @neyuki/ui
libraries.doc:
Windows, 2D drawing, input events and animation on Windows, macOS, X11 and Wayland from one code path. Frames are drawn on the CPU (no GPU or GL needed). The script owns the loop: `ui.poll` returns what happened, drawing calls paint a back buffer and `window:present()` shows it; `ui.run` wraps that loop.

Coordinates are logical pixels (HiDPI scaling is handled underneath). Colors are `"#rgb"`, `"#rrggbb"` or `"#rrggbbaa"` strings, `{ r, g, b, a? }` tables with channels from 0 to 255, or packed `0xRRGGBBAA` integers.

```lua
local ui = require("@neyuki/ui")
local win = ui.open({ title = "Hello", width = 480, height = 320 })
local ball = { x = 60, y = 160 }
ui.animate(ball, { x = 420 }, 1.5, { easing = "inOutSine", ["repeat"] = true, yoyo = true })

ui.run(function(events, dt)
    for _, event in events do
        if event.kind == "keydown" and event.key == "escape" then win:close() end
    end
    win:clear("#202030")
    win:circle(ball.x, ball.y, 24, "#4488ff")
    win:text(20, 20, "Press Escape to quit", { size = 18, color = "#ffffff" })
    win:present()
end)
```

entries.name: coroutine.create
entries.doc: A new suspended coroutine that will run `f`. The handle is frozen, and only it can resume the coroutine.

entries.name: coroutine.resume
entries.doc: Starts or continues `co`, passing the arguments to `f` (the first time) or as the results of `yield`. Returns `true` and the values passed to `yield` or returned by `f`, or `false` and the error message if it failed.

entries.name: coroutine.yield
entries.doc: Suspends the running coroutine, handing the arguments to `resume`. Returns the arguments of the next `resume`.

entries.name: coroutine.wrap
entries.doc: Creates a coroutine and returns a function that resumes it, returning what it yields and raising its errors.

entries.name: coroutine.status
entries.doc: `"suspended"`, `"running"`, `"normal"` (it resumed another coroutine) or `"dead"`.

entries.name: coroutine.running
entries.doc: The running coroutine (or `nil` in the main program) and whether that is the main program.

entries.name: coroutine.isyieldable
entries.doc: Whether `yield` would succeed here.

entries.name: coroutine.close
entries.doc: Kills a suspended or finished coroutine and frees its stack. Returns `true`, or `false` and a message for one that is still running.

entries.name: crypto.hash
entries.signature: crypto.hash(s: string, algorithm: string?, encoding: string?): string
entries.doc:
The digest of `s` with `"sha256"` (default), `"sha224"`, `"sha384"`, `"sha512"`, `"sha3-256"`, `"sha3-512"`, `"blake2b"`, `"blake2s"`, `"sha1"` or `"md5"`.

```lua
print(crypto.hash("hello")) --> 2cf24dba5fb0a30e26e83b2ac5b9e29e1b161e5c1fa7425e73043362938b9824
```

entries.name: crypto.hmac
entries.signature: crypto.hmac(s: string, key: string, algorithm: string?, encoding: string?): string
entries.doc: A keyed digest (HMAC) of `s`, with the same algorithms as `hash` except BLAKE2.

entries.name: crypto.equals
entries.doc: Compares two strings in constant time. Use it for MACs and tokens so the comparison does not reveal how much matched.

entries.name: crypto.hashPassword
entries.doc: A salted, self-describing password hash. `options.algorithm` is `"argon2id"` (default; `cost`, `memory` in KiB and `parallelism` default to 2, 19456 and 1) or `"bcrypt"` (`cost` defaults to 12; passwords over 72 bytes are refused).

entries.name: crypto.verifyPassword
entries.doc: Whether `password` matches a hash from `hashPassword` (either algorithm).

entries.name: crypto.pbkdf2
entries.signature: crypto.pbkdf2(password: string, salt: string, options: table?): string
entries.doc: Derives a key from a password with PBKDF2. `options` may set `algorithm`, `iterations` (default 600000), `length` in bytes (default 32) and `encoding`.

entries.name: crypto.hkdf
entries.doc: Derives a key from key material with HKDF. `options` may set `algorithm`, `salt`, `info`, `length` and `encoding` (which also applies to `key`).

entries.name: crypto.generateKey
entries.doc: A random key for `"aes-256-gcm"` (default), `"aes-128-gcm"`, `"chacha20-poly1305"` or `"xchacha20-poly1305"`.

entries.name: crypto.encrypt
entries.signature: crypto.encrypt(s: string, key: string, options: table?): string
entries.doc: Seals `s` with an authenticated cipher and a fresh random nonce, returning `nonce || ciphertext || tag`. `options` may hold `algorithm`, `aad` (data that is authenticated but not encrypted, which `decrypt` must be given again) and `encoding` (of the key and the result).

entries.name: crypto.decrypt
entries.signature: crypto.decrypt(s: string, key: string, options: table?): string
entries.doc: Opens what `encrypt` sealed. Raises an error for a wrong key or tampered data.

entries.name: crypto.generateKeyPair
entries.doc: `{ publicKey, privateKey }` for `"ed25519"` (default), `"x25519"` or `"rsa"` (`options.bits` defaults to 2048).

entries.name: crypto.publicKey
entries.doc: The public half of a private key.

entries.name: crypto.sign
entries.signature: crypto.sign(s: string, privateKey: string, options: table?): string
entries.doc:
Signs `s` with an Ed25519 or RSA key. For RSA, `options` may set `hash` (default `"sha256"`) and `padding` (`"pss"`, the default, or `"pkcs1"`).

```lua
local keys = crypto.generateKeyPair()
local signature = crypto.sign("release-1.0.zip", keys.privateKey)
assert(crypto.verify("release-1.0.zip", signature, keys.publicKey))
```

entries.name: crypto.verify
entries.signature: crypto.verify(s: string, signature: string, publicKey: string, options: table?): boolean
entries.doc: Whether `signature` is valid for `s`. Returns `false` for a bad or malformed signature. A private key is accepted in place of the public one.

entries.name: crypto.publicEncrypt
entries.signature: crypto.publicEncrypt(s: string, publicKey: string, options: table?): string
entries.doc: Encrypts a short message, such as a symmetric key, with RSA-OAEP.

entries.name: crypto.privateDecrypt
entries.signature: crypto.privateDecrypt(s: string, privateKey: string, options: table?): string

entries.name: crypto.uuid

entries.signature: debug.sethook(hook: function?, mask: string?, count: number?): ()

```lua

```

entries.name: http.request
entries.doc:
Performs one request. `options` may hold `method` (default `"GET"`), `headers` (a `{ name = value }` table), `body`, `timeout` (seconds for the whole exchange; unlimited by default), `follow` (whether to follow redirects; default `true`) and `maxBody` (the largest response body accepted, default 64 MiB).

Only transport failures (DNS, connection, TLS, timeout) raise errors. Every status code comes back as a `Response` with `status`, `ok` (true for 2xx), `headers` (names lower-cased), `body`, `url` (after redirects) and `header(name)`, a case-insensitive lookup.

entries.name: http.get
entries.doc: A `GET` request.

entries.name: http.head
entries.doc: A `HEAD` request.

entries.name: http.delete
entries.doc: A `DELETE` request.

entries.name: http.post
entries.signature: http.post(url: string, body: string?, options: table?): Response

entries.name: http.put
entries.signature: http.put(url: string, body: string?, options: table?): Response
entries.doc: A `PUT` request with `body`.

entries.name: http.patch
entries.signature: http.patch(url: string, body: string?, options: table?): Response
entries.doc: A `PATCH` request with `body`.

entries.name: http.encode
entries.doc: Percent-encodes a string for use in a URL.

entries.name: http.decode
entries.doc: Reverses `encode`.

entries.name: http.query
entries.doc:
Builds an `a=1&b=2` query string from a table, sorted by key.

```lua
http.get("https://example.com/search?" .. http.query({ q = "snow", page = 2 }))
```

entries.name: http.parseQuery
entries.doc: Splits a `path?query` target into the path and a table of decoded parameters.

entries.name: http.listen
entries.doc:
Binds a server. `options` is a port or `{ host?, port?, maxBody? }`, defaulting to `127.0.0.1`, port `8080` and 64 MiB; port `0` picks a free one. A request whose body is over `maxBody` is answered with 413 and never returned.

The `Server` has `host`, `port`, `url`, `accept(timeout?)` (the next `Request`, or `nil` once `timeout` seconds pass without one), `isOpen()` and `close()`.

A `Request` has `method`, `path`, `headers`, `body`, `remote`, `header(name)`, `query()` (the path and its decoded parameters), `forward(target, options?)` and `respond(reply)`. `respond` may be called once, with `nil` (204), a string (200, `text/plain`) or `{ status?, headers?, body? }`.

entries.name: http.serve
entries.signature: http.serve(options: number | table?, handler: (Request) -> any): never
entries.doc:
Runs `listen` and calls `handler(request)` for every request, forever, sending its return value with `respond` unless the handler already answered. A handler error is printed to standard error and answered with a 500.

```lua
http.serve(8080, function(request)
    local path, params = request:query()
    if path == "/hello" then return "hello " .. (params.name ?? "world") end
    if path == "/api/time" then
        return { headers = { ["content-type"] = "application/json" }, body = json.encode({ now = os.time() }) }
    end
    return { status = 404, body = "not found" }
end)
```

entries.name: http.forward
entries.signature: http.forward(options: number | table?, target: number | table): Forward
entries.doc:
A TCP port forward: binds `options` (as for `listen`) and relays every connection to `target` (a local port or `{ host?, port }`) byte for byte, so HTTP, WebSockets and TLS all pass through. Relaying runs on background threads. The `Forward` has `host`, `port`, `url`, `target`, `isOpen()`, `close()` and `wait(timeout?)`, which blocks for `timeout` seconds or for as long as the forward runs.

```lua
http.forward(1234, 5173):wait() -- expose a dev server on port 1234
```

`request:forward(target, options?)` answers a single request with whatever `target` (a port, `{ host?, port }` or a base URL) replies, passing the method, path, headers and body through unchanged; `options.timeout` bounds the upstream call. If the upstream cannot be reached the client gets a 502 and the error is raised. WebSocket upgrades need `http.forward` instead.

entries.name: io.read
entries.doc:
Reads from standard input, one value per format: `"l"` a line without its newline (the default), `"L"` a line with its newline, `"a"` everything remaining, `"n"` a whitespace-delimited number, or a number of characters. Each format yields `nil` once input runs out.

```lua
local width, height = io.read("n", "n")
```

entries.name: io.lines
entries.doc: An iterator that reads with `format` (default `"l"`) until input runs out.

entries.name: io.write
entries.doc: Writes the arguments to standard output with no separators or trailing newline, and returns `io.stdout` so calls chain.

entries.name: io.prompt

entries.name: io.stdin
entries.doc: Standard input, with the methods `read(...)`, `lines(format?)` and `isTerminal()`.

entries.name: io.stdout
entries.doc: Standard output, with the methods `write(...)`, `flush()` and `isTerminal()`.

entries.name: io.stderr
entries.doc:

A table whose metatable has `__tojson` is encoded as whatever that function returns. Raises an error for functions, cycles, NaN or infinity, and output over 64 MiB.

```lua

```

entries.doc:


entries.name: os.time
entries.doc:
Whole seconds since the Unix epoch (1970-01-01 UTC). Given a table with `year`, `month`, `day` and optionally `hour` (default 12), `min` and `sec`, returns that local time instead. Fields out of range carry over, so `month = 13` is January of the next year.

```lua
local deadline = os.time({ year = 2026, month = 12, day = 24, hour = 18 })
print(os.difftime(deadline, os.time()) // 86400, "days left")
```

entries.name: os.date
entries.signature: os.date(format: string?, time: number?): string | table
entries.doc:
Formats `time` (default: now, in seconds since the epoch) in local time with strftime codes: `%Y` year, `%m` month, `%d` day, `%H` `%M` `%S` time, `%A`/`%a` weekday name, `%B`/`%b` month name, `%j` day of the year, `%Z` time zone and `%%` a percent sign, among others. The default format is `"%c"`. A leading `!` formats in UTC, and `"*t"` (or `"!*t"`) returns a table with `year`, `month`, `day`, `hour`, `min`, `sec`, `wday` (Sunday is 1) and `yday`.

```lua
print(os.date("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"))          --> 2026-10-13 22:19
print(os.date("!%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", 0))  --> 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z
local today = os.date("*t")
print(today.year, today.month, today.day)
```

entries.name: os.run
entries.doc:
Runs a program, waits for it and returns `{ ok, code, stdout, stderr }`, where `ok` is true for exit code 0. A string runs through the system shell (`cmd /C` on Windows, `sh -c` elsewhere), so pipes and redirection work; a list runs its first element with the rest as arguments and no shell, so nothing needs quoting. `options` may hold `cwd` (the directory to run in), `env` (a table of variables to add or override), `stdin` (text to feed the program) and `capture` (default `true`; `false` lets the output go straight to the terminal). A program that cannot be started raises an error; one that fails just returns `ok = false`.

```lua
local result = os.run({ "git", "log", "--oneline", "-5" })
if result.ok then print(result.stdout) else print("git failed: " .. result.stderr) end

os.run("cargo build --release", { cwd = "../engine", capture = false })
```

entries.name: sql.connect
entries.doc: Connects to a database. `target` is a URL (`"postgres://user:pass@host:5432/db"`, `"mysql://user:pass@host/db"`) or a table with `driver` (`"postgres"` or `"mysql"`), `host`, `port`, `user`, `password`, `database`, `ssl` and `timeout` (seconds to wait). A table may also carry `url`, with its other fields overriding parts of it. TLS is required for any host other than this machine unless `ssl` is `false` (or a PostgreSQL URL sets `sslmode`).

entries.name: Connection:query
entries.doc: Runs a statement and returns its rows as an array of `{ column = value }` tables. `rows.columns` lists the column names in order.

entries.name: Connection:queryOne
entries.doc: The first row of the result, or `nil`.

entries.name: Connection:execute
entries.doc: Runs a statement for its effect and returns the number of rows it touched, then the auto-increment id of a MySQL insert. Without parameters the statement uses the simple protocol, so `BEGIN` and schema changes work everywhere.

entries.name: Connection:transaction
entries.doc:
Runs `body(connection)` in a transaction: commits when it returns, rolls back and re-raises when it fails, and returns what `body` returned.

```lua
db:transaction(function(tx)
    tx:execute("UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - $1 WHERE id = $2", { 25, 1 })
    tx:execute("UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + $1 WHERE id = $2", { 25, 2 })
end)
```

entries.name: Connection:begin
entries.doc: Starts a transaction by hand.

entries.name: Connection:commit
entries.doc: Commits the transaction started with `begin`.

entries.name: Connection:rollback
entries.doc: Rolls back the transaction started with `begin`.

entries.name: Connection:ping
entries.doc: Whether the server still answers.

entries.name: Connection:close
entries.doc: Closes the connection. Calling it again does nothing.

entries.name: Connection:isOpen
entries.doc: Whether the connection has not been closed.

entries.name: string.len
entries.doc: The length in bytes, the same as `#s`.

entries.name: string.count
entries.doc:
The number of characters (Unicode code points).

```lua
print(#"héllo", string.count("héllo")) --> 6	5
```

entries.name: string.sub
entries.signature: string.sub(s: string, i: number, j: number?): string
entries.doc:
The substring from byte `i` to byte `j` (default: the end), both inclusive.

```lua
print(("neyuki"):sub(1, 3), ("neyuki"):sub(-2)) --> ney	ki
```

entries.name: string.upper
entries.doc: `s` in upper case, including non-ASCII letters.

entries.name: string.lower
entries.doc: `s` in lower case, including non-ASCII letters.

entries.name: string.rep
entries.signature: string.rep(s: string, n: number, sep: string?): string
entries.doc: `s` repeated `n` times, with `sep` between the copies.

entries.name: string.reverse
entries.doc: `s` with its bytes in reverse order.

entries.name: string.split
entries.doc:
Splits `s` at every occurrence of `separator` (plain text, default `","`). An empty separator splits into characters.

```lua
local parts = ("a,b,,c"):split(",") --> { "a", "b", "", "c" }
```

entries.name: string.trim
entries.doc: `s` without leading and trailing whitespace, or without any of the characters in `chars`.

entries.name: string.ltrim
entries.doc: Like `trim`, but only at the start.

entries.name: string.rtrim
entries.doc: Like `trim`, but only at the end.

entries.name: string.startswith
entries.doc: Whether `s` begins with `prefix`.

entries.name: string.endswith
entries.doc: Whether `s` ends with `suffix`.

entries.name: string.find
entries.signature: string.find(s: string, pattern: string, init: number?, plain: boolean?): (number?, number?, ...string)
entries.doc:
The start and end of the first match of `pattern` at or after `init`, followed by its captures, or `nil`. With `plain`, `pattern` is plain text.

```lua
print(("hello world"):find("o w")) --> 5	7
```

entries.name: string.match
entries.signature: string.match(s: string, pattern: string, init: number?): ...string?
entries.doc:
The captures of the first match (or the whole match when the pattern has none), or `nil`.

```lua
local key, value = ("name=neyuki"):match("(%w+)=(%w+)")
```

entries.name: string.gmatch
entries.doc:
An iterator over every match, yielding its captures or the whole match.

```lua
for word in ("one two three"):gmatch("%a+") do print(word) end
```

entries.name: string.gsub
entries.signature: string.gsub(s: string, pattern: string, replacement: string | table | function, n: number?): (string, number)
entries.doc:
`s` with every match (or the first `n`) replaced, and the number of replacements. A string replacement may refer to captures as `%1` to `%9` (`%0` is the whole match); a table is indexed with the first capture; a function is called with the captures. A `nil` or `false` result keeps the match.

```lua
print(("hello world"):gsub("o", "0"))            --> hell0 w0rld	2
print(("$name!"):gsub("%$(%w+)", { name = "Yuki" })) --> Yuki!	1
```

entries.name: string.format
entries.doc:
Builds a string from a C-style template: `%d` and `%i` integers, `%f`, `%e` and `%g` floats, `%x`/`%X` hexadecimal, `%o` octal, `%c` a character code, `%s` any value through `tostring`, `%q` a quoted literal and `%%` a percent sign. Flags, width and precision work as in C (`%-8s`, `%05.2f`).

```lua
print(string.format("%-6s|%5.1f|%x", "id", 3.14159, 255)) --> id    |  3.1|ff
```

entries.name: string.byte
entries.signature: string.byte(s: string, i: number?, j: number?): ...number
entries.doc: The byte values from `i` (default 1) to `j` (default `i`).

entries.name: string.char
entries.doc: A string made of the given byte values.

entries.name: string.pack
entries.doc: Packs values into a binary string, one character per byte. The format uses Lua's codes: `<` `>` `=` set byte order, `b`/`B` 8-bit, `h`/`H` 16-bit, `i[n]`/`I[n]` and `j`/`J` integers, `f`/`d`/`n` floats, `s[n]` length-prefixed strings, `z` zero-terminated strings and `x` padding.

entries.name: string.packsize
entries.doc: The size of the string `pack` produces for `format`, which may not contain variable-length options.

entries.name: string.unpack
entries.signature: string.unpack(format: string, s: string, init: number?): ...any
entries.doc: Reads the values `pack` wrote, followed by the position after the last byte read.

entries.name: table.insert
table.remove
entries.doc: Removes and returns the element at `pos` (default: the last one), shifting the later elements down.

entries.name: table.concat
entries.signature: table.concat(t: {any}, sep: string?, i: number?, j: number?): string
entries.doc:
Joins the strings and numbers `t[i]` to `t[j]` (default: the whole array) with `sep` between them.

```lua
print(table.concat({ 1, 2, 3 }, ", ")) --> 1, 2, 3
```

entries.name: table.sort
entries.doc:
Sorts the array in place with `<`, or with `comp(a, b)` returning true when `a` must come before `b`. The sort is stable: equal elements keep their order.

```lua
table.sort(people, function(a, b) return a.age < b.age end)
```

entries.name: table.find
entries.signature: table.find(t: {any}, value: any, init: number?): any
entries.doc: The first index in the array part (from `init`) holding `value`, then any other key holding it, or `nil`.

entries.name: table.create
entries.doc: An array of `n` copies of `value`.

entries.name: table.length
entries.doc: The number of non-nil entries, named keys included.

entries.name: table.keys
entries.doc: A new array of every key: array indices first, then string keys in sorted order, then the rest.

entries.name: table.values
entries.doc: A new array of every value, in the same order as `keys`.

entries.name: table.clone
entries.doc: A shallow copy that shares `t`'s metatable. The copy is never frozen.

entries.name: table.clear
entries.doc: Removes every entry from `t`.

entries.name: table.freeze
entries.doc: Makes `t` read-only (writes raise an error) and returns it. Freezing is shallow: tables inside `t` stay writable.

entries.name: table.isfrozen
entries.doc: Whether `t` is frozen.

entries.name: table.pack
entries.doc: An array of the arguments with the field `n` set to their count, `nil`s included.

entries.name: table.unpack
entries.doc:
Returns `t[i]` to `t[j]` (default: the whole array) as separate values.

```lua
local x, y = table.unpack({ 10, 20 })
```

entries.name: table.move
entries.signature: table.move(a1: {any}, f: number, e: number, t: number, a2: {any}?): {any}
entries.doc: Copies `a1[f..e]` to `a2[t..]` (or within `a1`), handling overlap, and returns the destination.

entries.name: ui.open
entries.doc: Opens a window. `options` may hold `title` (default `"Neyuki"`), `width` and `height` (default 800 × 600), `resizable` (default `true`) and `visible` (default `true`). The canvas starts out white.

entries.name: ui.run
entries.signature: ui.run(handler: (events: {table}, dt: number) -> any, options: table?): ()
entries.doc: Calls `handler(events, dt)` about 60 times a second (`options.fps`) until every window is closed, where `dt` is the seconds since the previous call. Tweens from `ui.animate` are stepped just before each call. Close requests close their window unless `options.autoClose` is `false`. An error in the handler closes the windows and is raised again.

entries.name: ui.poll
entries.doc:
Pumps the event loop and returns the events since the last call. Without a timeout it returns at once; with one it waits up to that many seconds for the first event. Each event has `kind` and `window` plus:

- `close`: the close button or shortcut was used (call `window:close()` to honour it)
- `resize`: `width`, `height`
- `focus`, `blur`, `redraw`, `mouseenter`, `mouseleave`
- `keydown`, `keyup`: `key` (`"a"`, `"escape"`, `"arrowleft"`, `"f1"`), `code` (`"KeyA"`), `repeat`, `text`, `mods` (`shift`, `ctrl`, `alt`, `meta`)
- `mousemove`: `x`, `y`
- `mousedown`, `mouseup`: `button` (`"left"`, `"right"`, `"middle"`), `x`, `y`
- `scroll`: `dx`, `dy`, `unit` (`"lines"` or `"pixels"`), `x`, `y`

entries.name: ui.isAvailable
entries.doc: Whether a display can be reached. On a headless machine the other window functions raise an error.

entries.name: ui.color
entries.doc: Packs any color form into a `0xRRGGBBAA` integer, to avoid re-parsing a color every frame.

entries.name: ui.loadFont
entries.doc: Loads a TrueType or OpenType font for `text` and `measureText`. Without one, text uses the bundled Noto Sans. `font:close()` frees it.

entries.name: ui.loadImage
entries.doc: Decodes a PNG file into an `Image` with `width` and `height`. `image:close()` frees it.

entries.name: ui.measureText
entries.doc: The width and height `window:text` would cover for `s`, with the same `size` and `font` options.

entries.name: Window:clear
entries.doc: Fills the whole canvas (default white).

entries.name: Window:fillRect
entries.signature: Window:fillRect(x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number, color: any, options: table?): ()
entries.doc: A filled rectangle; `options.radius` rounds the corners.

entries.name: Window:strokeRect
entries.signature: Window:strokeRect(x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number, color: any, options: table?): ()
entries.doc: A rectangle outline; `options.width` is the line width and `options.radius` rounds the corners.

entries.name: Window:line
entries.signature: Window:line(x1: number, y1: number, x2: number, y2: number, color: any, options: table?): ()
entries.doc: A line; `options.width` is its width.

entries.name: Window:circle
entries.signature: Window:circle(cx: number, cy: number, radius: number, color: any, options: table?): ()
entries.doc: A filled circle, or an outline of `options.width` when `options.fill` is `false`.

entries.name: Window:polygon
entries.doc: A closed shape through the points of a flat `{ x1, y1, x2, y2, ... }` list, filled unless `options.fill` is `false`.

entries.name: Window:text
entries.signature: Window:text(x: number, y: number, s: string, options: table?): number
entries.doc: Draws text with the top-left corner of its first line at `(x, y)`; `"\n"` starts a new line. `options` may hold `size` (default 16), `color` (default black) and `font`. Returns the width drawn.

entries.name: Window:drawImage
entries.signature: Window:drawImage(image: Image, x: number, y: number, options: table?): ()
entries.doc: Draws an image at its own size, or scaled to `options.width` and/or `options.height`.

entries.name: Window:present
entries.doc: Shows everything drawn since the last call.

entries.name: Window:size
entries.doc: The current logical width and height.

entries.name: Window:setSize
entries.doc: Resizes the window.

entries.name: Window:scale
entries.doc: Physical pixels per logical pixel (2 on a typical HiDPI display).

entries.name: Window:title
entries.doc: The window title.

entries.name: Window:setTitle
entries.doc: Changes the window title.

entries.name: Window:isOpen
entries.doc: Whether the window has not been closed.

entries.name: Window:close
entries.doc: Closes the window. Calling it again does nothing.

entries.name: ui.tween
entries.signature: ui.tween(target: table, goal: table, duration: number, options: table?): Tween
entries.doc:
Animates the fields of `target` toward the values in `goal` over `duration` seconds. Number fields move numerically; any other goal is a color, and the field ends up a packed color. Starting values are read when the tween starts, so a tween chained from `onComplete` continues where the previous one ended.

`options` may hold `easing` (a function or the name of a `ui.easing` curve, default `"outQuad"`), `delay` (seconds), `repeat` (extra runs, or `true` for forever), `yoyo` (alternate runs play backwards), `onUpdate(target)` and `onComplete(target)`.

A `Tween` does nothing until `tween:update(dt)` is called, which returns whether it has ended. It also has `pause()`, `resume()`, `cancel()` (stop in place), `finish()` (jump to the goal and call `onComplete`), `isDone()`, `isPaused()` and `progress()` (0 to 1).

entries.name: ui.animate
entries.signature: ui.animate(target: table, goal: table, duration: number, options: table?): Tween
entries.doc:
Like `tween`, but registered so `ui.run` (or `ui.update`) steps it until it ends.

```lua
local panel = { y = -200, fill = "#334455" }
ui.animate(panel, { y = 0 }, 0.4, { easing = "outBack" })
ui.animate(panel, { fill = "#5577aa" }, 0.8, { delay = 0.4 })
```

entries.name: ui.update
entries.doc: Steps every tween started with `animate` by `dt` seconds and returns how many are still running. Only needed in a loop written with `poll` instead of `run`.

entries.name: ui.easing
entries.doc: Easing curves that map progress from 0 to 1: `linear`, `inQuad`, `outQuad`, `inOutQuad`, `inCubic`, `outCubic`, `inOutCubic`, `inSine`, `outSine`, `inOutSine`, `inExpo`, `outExpo`, `inBack`, `outBack`, `outElastic` and `outBounce`.

entries.name: ui.lerp
entries.signature: ui.lerp(a: number, b: number, t: number): number
entries.doc: The value `t` of the way from `a` to `b`.

entries.name: ui.mixColor
entries.signature: ui.mixColor(from: any, to: any, t: number): number
entries.doc: Mixes two colors channel by channel, alpha included, and returns the packed result.

entries.name: utf8.len
entries.signature: utf8.len(s: string, i: number?, j: number?): number
entries.doc: How many characters start between byte positions `i` (default 1) and `j` (default -1).

entries.name: utf8.char
entries.doc:
The string made of the given code points.

```lua
print(utf8.char(72, 233)) --> Hé
```

entries.name: utf8.codepoint
entries.signature: utf8.codepoint(s: string, i: number?, j: number?): ...number
entries.doc: The code points of the characters that start between byte positions `i` (default 1) and `j` (default `i`).

entries.name: utf8.offset
entries.signature: utf8.offset(s: string, n: number, i: number?): number?
entries.doc: The byte position where the `n`th character counting from byte `i` starts, or `nil`. A negative `n` counts backwards and `n = 0` finds the start of the character containing byte `i`.

entries.name: utf8.sub
entries.signature: utf8.sub(s: string, i: number, j: number?): string
entries.doc:
The characters from the `i`th to the `j`th (default: the last), counted like `string.sub` counts bytes.

```lua
print(utf8.sub("héllo", 2, 3)) --> él
```

entries.name: utf8.codes
entries.doc:
An iterator over the byte position and code point of each character.

```lua
for position, code in utf8.codes("hé") do print(position, code) end
```

entries.name: utf8.chars
entries.doc:
An iterator over each character as a string.

```lua
for char in utf8.chars("héllo") do print(char) end
```
